declared_parameter_provenance.decision: Use the Visante versus contact SL-US comparison only. The source included 50 eyes from 30 healthy volunteers, excluded prior ocular surgery and corneal pathology, and measured both instruments in the same eyes.

declared_parameter_provenance.source: PMC3343442, Methods: Subjects; Results: age 27.0 ± 2.9 years.
declared_parameter_provenance.decision: Treat the adult match as conditional. Mean age and SD do not prove that every participant was at least 18.

declared_parameter_provenance.source: PMC3343442, Results: Agreement among RTVue, Visante, and SL-US measurements.
declared_parameter_provenance.decision: Visante measured thinner than SL-US by 3.6 um; retain the OCT-minus-ultrasound sign.

declared_parameter_provenance.source: PMC3343442, Results: reported largest likely Visante–SL-US difference of 14.9 um; Statistics: corrected SD and Bland–Altman limits.
declared_parameter_provenance.decision: Interpret 14.9 um as the larger absolute endpoint of symmetric mean ± 1.96 SD limits. Then SD=(14.9-3.6)/1.96 and endpoints are -14.9 and 7.7 um. Actual Table 3 cells and Figure 3 are absent from the supplied material, so this reconstruction remains conditional.

declared_parameter_provenance.source: Modeling assumption informed by the article's Bland–Altman analysis.
declared_parameter_provenance.decision: Use normal, constant-variance differences. The aggregate article does not establish normal far tails.

declared_parameter_provenance.source: Virtual-cohort construction, not an article estimate.
declared_parameter_provenance.decision: Use only to construct paired absolute thickness columns; do not interpret as reconstructed source marginals.
Count only absolute differences strictly greater than 20 um.
Preserve the same difference mean and SD while allowing heavier tails.
